successors.name: Roman Republic
successors.text: the Cenomani country without the Latin colony of Cremona

ledger.x: The Cenomani settle between the Oglio and the Adige in 'the migrations of the late 5th and 4th centuries BC'; Williams has the settlement 'no later than the early 4th century BC'.
218 BC: Rome plants Cremona on Cenoman land.
89 BC: the Cenomani receive Latin rights.
89 BC: the Cenomani cease to stand apart as an allied people; Cisalpine Gaul gets citizenship in 49 BC and is merged into Italia about 42 BC.

wars.name: Cisalpine Gallic revolt (200-197 BC)
wars.outcome: 'By 200 BC the Cenomani had gone over to the anti-Roman side', joining the Boii and Insubres in the assault on Placentia; in 197 Roman envoys secured at least their neutrality and 'the Insubres were routed'.

certainty.note: The Po, the Oglio, the Alpine foothills and the Tartaro or Adige are the only limits the page gives.
